correctness.rationale: For m=12h−6≥6 the branch set is {0,∞} plus the roots of t^m=−1. Its reduced group contains rotation of order m and inversion; the finite subgroups of PGL₂(C) admitting order ≥6 are cyclic or dihedral, and inversion conjugates the rotation to its distinct inverse. Hence the full reduced group is dihedral: its rotation part fixes 0,∞, and scales preserving the m roots have order dividing m. The lifts ρ=(ξ²t,ξy), for ξ of order 2m, and s=(1/t,y/t^{(m+2)/2}) lift both generators; ρ^m is the hyperelliptic involution, and substitution gives sρs=ρ^(m−1). In the noncyclic coset (ρ^a s)²=ρ^(ma), so the order-three subgroup A is unique and all candidates are <A,ρ^(2j)s>. Each is S₃ because s inverts A. Its index j is unique mod m/3=2k with k=2h−1. Conjugation by ρ adds 1−3k, of gcd 2 with 2k; conjugation by s multiplies j by m−1 and preserves parity. Thus there are 2k subgroups, k in each conjugacy class, with representatives s and ρ^m s. A fixes only the two points over 0 and ∞, which are exchanged by either reflection. The plus reflection fixes four points over t=±1, the minus none. Distinct plus transpositions cannot have a common fixed point, since their product is a nontrivial element of A and neither fixes a point in the A-fixed pair. The contributions to Riemann–Hurwitz are therefore 4+12 and 4, giving genera h−1 and h. Independently, t³ and ty generate the order-three fixed field, and in that field x+x⁻¹ together with the stated signed invariants gives index two for each reflection. P_{2h−1} has 2h−1 distinct roots obtained by pairing inverse roots of x^(4h−2)=−1, none at ±2. This also checks the h=1 endpoint.
residual_risks: Only complex-curve automorphisms and conjugation in the full complex automorphism group are classified; the same proof does not assert a rational form or positive-characteristic classification.

residual_risks: The combined primary-literature lookup surfaced no additional result; this is not negative evidence. Classical subgroup-action classifications for large hyperelliptic automorphism groups may contain an equivalent census under a different group presentation.

value.rationale: On a naturally specified unbounded-genus family previously studied for one S₃ action, the census specifies all conjugacy classes of the same acting group, and the inertia dichotomy determines exactly which actions give each quotient genus. This answers a finite-group action classification uniformly rather than merely giving another defining equation or another example. The known paired quotient equations alone are not the value claim.
residual_risks: Modest classification within one family; no novel general method, derived-category consequence, or extension to all dihedral covers is asserted.
